fields.h1: Build a Rental History Form That Reaches Every Past Landlord
fields.hero_description: Build a rental history form that collects each past address, then emails every previous landlord a short verification.
fields.features_heading: Both Halves of a Rental Check
fields.features_subheading: The applicant lists where they have lived. Each previous landlord confirms the dates and rent, then says how the tenancy ended.
fields.feature_1:
An address timeline that adds up

Applicants enter each address with move-in and move-out months. The form totals the months against the window you set and asks about any gap before it accepts the submission.
fields.feature_2:
A separate link for each past landlord

On submit, the app emails every landlord the applicant named a verification page that already shows the applicant's name, the rental address, and the dates they claimed.
fields.feature_3:
Short questions a landlord can answer

Ask for the monthly rent, late payments in the last 12 months, whether notice was given, and whether they would rent again. Yes-or-no answers fit the whole reply on one screen.
fields.feature_4:
A release the applicant signs first

Before the form submits, the applicant types a signature authorizing past landlords to share their rental history. A copy of the signed page goes with every verification request.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders and a status for each request

A landlord who has not replied after 2 days gets a reminder email. The leasing manager sees each request as sent, reminded, or returned, next to the applicant it belongs to.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, on your own GitHub

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans when the rental history form needs to sit inside an existing leasing system. Host it anywhere and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Sides of One Rental History Check
fields.tab_content_1:
Four missing months get explained, or the form waits

Wendell Torvik rents out a fourplex on Larkspur Street and asks for 36 months of addresses. Rosalind Achebe lists 2 apartments that cover 32 of the 36. The form flags the 4-month gap and holds her submission until she explains it. She stayed with her brother between leases, and says so.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two replies in, and the third landlord hears again

Jonah Whitlock applies at Kestrel Row Apartments and names 3 previous landlords. The app emails each of them a verification link, and 2 of the 3 reply by evening. Harlan Pruitt has not answered after 2 days, so he gets a reminder email. Corinne Valdivia, the leasing manager, sees his request marked reminded.
fields.tab_content_3:
Her old landlord answers six questions on a phone

Ines Farrowby rented a duplex unit to Dmitri Sandoval for 26 months, and she opens the verification link on her phone. She confirms the dates and the $1,450 monthly rent, reports 1 late payment in the last 12 months, and says he gave written notice. His deposit came back in full, and she would rent to him again.
fields.tab_content_4:
The applicant with no lease names her campus housing

Talulah Brennick has never held a lease of her own. Answering no to the rented-before question opens a section for her 2 years in campus housing at Thornbury Hall. The app sends her resident director, Orrin Castellano, a 4-question version. It asks about her move-out inspection and any unpaid charges.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Rental History Form
fields.howto_description: Follow 7 steps to create a rental history form that covers each past address and gets a reply from every previous landlord.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick a window for past addresses
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for each address with its dates
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick a window, such as the last 36 months or the two most recent addresses, and print it at the top of the form. Applicants then know how far back to go, and the form has a number to check their timeline against.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give every address its own block: street, unit, move-in month, move-out month, and the landlord or manager's name, email, and phone. A month field is enough. Exact days add typing for the applicant and tell you nothing new.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a short authorization the applicant reads and signs by typing their name, giving past landlords permission to share their rental history. Write it in your own words and keep the signed page with the application.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Cap the landlord's page at six questions, and make each one a yes or no or a single number. The previous landlord is doing you a favor. A page that fits on one phone screen is the page that comes back.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put both sets of questions and the reminder timing into one prompt. Emergent builds the rental history form, the landlord's verification page, and the database behind them. Change any question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide who reads each returned verification, and how long to wait before a reminder. A leasing manager might see every request, while a slow reply waits 2 days for its nudge. Name a backup reader for vacation weeks.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a test applicant through it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Apply as a made-up tenant and list your own email as the previous landlord. Check that the verification link arrives, that your answers land on the right applicant, and that the reminder fires when you leave one request unanswered.

faq_plan.q: What is a rental history form?
faq_plan.a: A rental history form is how a landlord or property manager confirms where a rental applicant has lived. The applicant lists each past address with its dates and landlord. Each previous landlord then confirms the dates and rent, and says how the lease ended.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a rental history form?
faq_plan.a: Decide how many months of addresses to ask for, what each previous landlord should confirm, and who reads the replies. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the applicant's form, the page each landlord answers on, and the database behind both.

faq_plan.q: What should a rental history form template include?
faq_plan.a: Two halves. The applicant's half asks for each address in your window, with move-in and move-out months, the landlord's contact details, and a signed release. The landlord's half confirms the dates, the rent, the payment record, and the deposit. A rental history form template that skips either half leaves you making phone calls.

faq_plan.q: Is a free rental history form enough for a small landlord?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for a few units a free rental history form does the job if it covers every address in your window and gets each previous landlord's answers in writing. Keep the lease terms out of it: those belong on a rental agreement form, signed once the history checks out. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing the form.

faq_plan.q: How far back should a rental history form go?
faq_plan.a: Go back at least 36 months. When that window holds only one address, ask for the one before it as well, which gives you a second landlord to hear from. Add a field for why the applicant left each place, since it explains a short stay without a phone call.

faq_plan.q: How do I send a rental history form to a previous landlord?
faq_plan.a: Have the form email each landlord the applicant lists a separate verification link, filled in with the applicant's name and the dates given. The landlord answers on one page, and the app files the reply with the right application. An app built with Emergent can also send a reminder email to anyone who has not replied.

faq_plan.q: Should a rental history form ask about damage to the unit?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but ask about outcomes, not opinions. Have the previous landlord say whether any of the deposit was kept, and for what: unpaid rent, cleaning, or repairs. If you are the landlord answering, the tenant's entries in your maintenance request form log show how they reported problems while they lived there.

faq_plan.q: How should a rental history form handle first-time renters?
faq_plan.a: Ask whether the applicant has rented before, and open a different section when the answer is no. Ask about campus housing or a family home, with one reference who can speak to it, such as a resident director. Send that reference a shorter set of questions, since there is no rent to confirm.

faq_plan.q: How do I confirm the previous landlord on a rental history form is genuine?
faq_plan.a: Search the address yourself and compare the owner or management company you find with the name the applicant gave. Call a management company on the number its own website lists, not the one typed on the form. Leave the rent blank on the landlord's page and let them supply the figure.

faq_plan.q: What happens to a rental history form after the tenant moves in?
faq_plan.a: Keep it with the tenant's record for as long as you keep the application. It holds the history you relied on and the signed release. In an app built with Emergent, it sits in a database you own, next to later records for the same unit, such as each service request form the tenant files.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is blank PDFs and Word templates (a city housing bureau's form, a realtors' association request, a property manager's verification sheet, template and e-sign sites) plus one landlord-software guide. Each is a sheet someone prints, faxes or emails, then chases by phone. This page wins with both halves as one working form: the applicant's half (every address for the last 3 years with move-in and move-out months, each previous landlord's contact, a typed release) and the previous landlord's half (dates, rent, late payments, how the tenancy ended, would they rent again), with the app emailing each landlord their own link, reminding after 2 days and filing every reply with the applicant's record.
